column1: # What runs each script here, so that a check nothing runs is a fault rather
# than a file. One row per script under scripts/, excluding git-hooks/.
# The roles are the origin repository's vocabulary, used unchanged so the two
# inventories stay readable side by side: suite, gated, workflow, library, tool.

column3: A repo wide guard. test-ci-workflow.sh drives it, and that suite runs on every push through run-tests.sh.
A repo wide guard. test-check-ported-artifacts.sh runs it against the real tree and the real siblings as one of its own cases, so a stale port turns the suite red on push.
Named by the CI workflow step, and by the pre push hook. It is the only thing that scans the REAL tree: the suite exercises it against throwaway trees only.
Run by hand, once per clone. Nothing automated may call it, because a hook a machine installed for you is one nobody chose.
The runner the pre push hook and the CI workflow both call. test-run-tests.sh drives it against throwaway trees.
Sourced by check-ported-artifacts.sh and check-ported-content.sh. Never run.
Sourced first by check-ci-workflow.sh and check-ported-artifacts.sh, to load every other library or refuse by name (ovation#399, backstage#69). Never run.
The one reader of this file. Sourced by check-ci-workflow.sh. Never run.
Sourced by every suite. test-test-harness.sh covers it.
Sourced by check-ci-workflow.sh to decide what counts as a step. Never run.
Covers check-ported-artifacts.sh.
Covers check-ci-workflow.sh.
Covers the pre push hook and install-git-hooks.sh, with real pushes to a real throwaway remote.
Covers run-tests.sh.
Covers check-secrets.sh.
Covers lib/test-harness.sh.
Proves a consumer naming no Gmail scopes does not compile, by building one (backstage#3).
Holds lib/script-roles.tsv to the scripts on disk, in both directions (backstage#10).
Refuses a script that spells a generated manifest's package identity or path out instead of deriving it (backstage#30).
Named by .github/workflows/secrets-history.yml. It reads every blob ever committed, which is the one question the working tree guard cannot answer (backstage#11).
Covers check-secrets-history.sh.
What counts as a credential or a real mailbox. Imported by check-secrets.sh and check-secrets-history.sh, so the two cannot disagree. Never run.
A repo wide guard. test-ported-content.sh runs it against the real tree and the real siblings as one of its own cases, so a port edited here turns the suite red on push (backstage#9).
Covers check-ported-content.sh.

Run by hand to cut a release (backstage#12, ovation#423). Nothing automated may call it: a tag is what other repositories pin to, so creating one is a decision somebody makes, never a consequence of a push.
Covers cut-release.sh. Every case drives one REFUSAL, because a tag other repositories pin to is the worst place for a stale green.
